stemMd: A cylindrical tank has radius 4 m and height 9 m. It is filled to one third of its height. What volume of water is in it?
explanationMd: Water depth is 9/3=3 m. Volume equals circular base area times depth, π times 4 squared times 3=48π cubic metres.

distractorRationale.c: This is the full tank volume.
distractorRationale.b: This is the base area's numerical value without water depth.
distractorRationale.a: This does not square the radius.
